note: One entry per claim. The layer is decided by what carries the capability, and the gate (scripts/check_layer_separation.py) rejects a claim whose module marker, path or evidence contradicts it.

claims.claim: A fact taught in conversation is recalled: same wording, a taught relation synonym, an English question, a correction, and 12 unrelated turns later.

evidence.method: Invented entities (absent from every corpus); cold -> teach -> same wording -> English -> unseen wording -> correction -> retention -> composition; per-turn answer source recorded.

result.value: recall 7/7 on every stage; cold 7/7 abstain; answers attributed with source=memory

claims.claim: The native engine (GARDEN) learns a fact from dialogue, i.e. the capability survives deletion of the text.

evidence.method: Teach 3 invented facts through the production learner (learn_from_interaction); ask; keep only the SNN checkpoint; ask again. No pipeline, router or memory layer involved.

result.value: cold 0%, taught 0%, after source deletion 0%; the objects are kept verbatim in dictionary.json and the learned pair is (statement -> canned reply)

claims.claim: Curated factual recall of public propositions, with a source.

evidence.method: Native bench: knowledge (15 items, keyword match) and knowledge_mc (40 items).

claims.claim: Extractive answers from an offline public corpus (Simple English Wikipedia, FTS5).

evidence.method: Same knowledge suite; the reader abstains when no retrieved sentence shares two content words with the question (the question's type word is no longer required inside the sentence — that filter discarded the answer sentences; type safety is enforced only in the definition-shaped entity path).

result.value: ablation 2026-10-24: full 8/15 vs curated-only 5/15 vs knowledge-off 0/15 — the layer contributes +3 answers on top of the curated store and abstains on the rest

claims.claim: Chooses a destination and a surface form; it is not a source of facts or of capability.

evidence.method: Per-turn source distribution only; the probe never treats a route as a correctness claim.

result.value: recorded so routing/templates can never be presented as knowledge or learning

claims.claim: A trained core carries a token string across a turn boundary inside its state and generation reads it back: exact match is 0.995 on names and values never seen in training, while zeroing the state or skipping the teaching turn collapses it to 0.000. It is a *mechanism* (how to copy through the state), not knowledge or language: the name selects nothing (wrong_name 0.994).

evidence.method: Teach `remember <name> = <value> .` (no loss) -> al_step(120 s) -> ask `<name> ?` -> generate `<value> .`; the value never appears in turn 2's input. Train/dev/held-out values are disjoint by construction and the leak check is mechanical. Controls: zero_state (same state object, same weights, same prompt, only `h` zeroed), cold (teaching turn skipped; same questions), wrong_name (teach A, ask an untaught B). source_deleted: no evaluation reads the training data or any text store at all - the only artifact is the checkpoint - and deleting the carried state removes the capability, so what remains is a weight-level mechanism rather than a stored string.

result.value: seed 20261114, 60 epochs: held-out exact 0.995 (3,000), dev 0.994; zero-state 0.000, cold 0.000; checkpoint reload reproduces 0.995/0.000. Limits: wrong_name 0.994 (single-slot carry, no keyed lookup), no-al_step 0.003 (not gap-invariant), closed CV alphabet (not language), not wired into production.

claims.claim: The same trained core holds two taught bindings in its state at once and the query selects which one to answer.

evidence.method: Two teaching turns (`ai_step` + `al_step(120 s)` each), then one query naming either taught key, then generate that key's value; the value never appears in the query turn. Round 7 (the registered structural change) added `SlotMemoryCore`: the same GRU plus four gate-written, attention-read slots, 134,124 params, same splits (identical digests). Evaluation reads only the checkpoint - no training text and no value store. `source_deleted` stays true: the only artifact is the checkpoint, and ablating the store removes the capability from the model rather than hiding the answer. Controls: same-parameter GRU (C3, 136,821 params), the same arm with the store ablated (C2), zero-every-state-tensor, zero-h-only, zero-store-only, cold (teaching turns skipped, same questions), `wrong_name` (teach two keys, ask a third).

result.value: Round 7 (seed 20261115, 100 epochs, xpu): `slots` dev 0.0007 / held-out 0.0000, `other_value_rate` 0.0000, i.e. it does not emit a taught value at all. Bars B1 0.60 / B2 0.30. The store is not the missing piece: linear readouts of the addressed content decode both taught values at 0.589/0.593 characters (chance 0.1333; full exact 0.008/0.010 vs chance 2.4e-6). Selection is: `distinct_read_slot_rate` 0.0000/0.0003, `read_cosine_between_asks` 0.9998, `attention_max_prob_mean` 0.97 - both questions read the same slot, confidently. Worse, the store actively hurts decoding: the same arm with the store ablated scores 0.1233 held-out (B7 gap is -0.1233, not +0.20). B8 passes (matched-parameter GRU 0.1557 < 0.30), so parameters are not the explanation. Earlier rounds: single-binding carry passes (0.995), two bindings over one 128-d state fails (0.0033/0.0100), wider `h` does not fix it. Reading: storage works, addressing by a global learned query collapses to a constant position, and the read-into-controller wiring breaks the decoder - the next variable is the addressing signal (per-turn keys), not capacity, width, or epochs.
